newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Sept 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After State and Territory leaders resolved last week that Commonwealth-State financial reform and wider tax reform should be at the top of the agenda at the November Council of Australian Governments meeting, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett intensified presure on the Federal Government to look into tax reform by saying the States expected change after the next Federal election. Page 1.

Following an altercation last week with Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston, Labor communications spokesperson Chris Schacht indicated the Opposition would not support fast-tracking the draft telecommunications bill. The Democrats have also theatened not to support the move, throwing investments in Australia's fast-growing telecommunications sector into doubt. Page 3.

According to a submission to this week's tax summit prepared by the Institute of Public Affairs, the growth of State taxes has created an urgent need for policy reform and more competition among jurisdictions is needed to constrain overall taxation. The roposal and others from business and community groups will be presented at a tax summit organised by the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the Australian Council of Social Service to be held in Canberra this Friday and Saturday. Page 5.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday said Australian society was no place for on-going, long-standing royal commissions, such as Queensland's Criminal Justice Commission and the New South Wales Independent Commission Against Corruption. Kennett also called for the National Crime Authority to be wound up, following his attack on the body in August after the acquittal of former Federal Liberal Party president John Elliott on fraud charges. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following informal talks with Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett at the Australian Football League final on Saturday, Prime Minister John Howard has revealed he is preparing to increase the Commonwealth's funding of the gun buyback scheme in an effort to ensure it overcomes a multi-million-dollar shortfall from the States. Page 1.

In what will be his first public appearance in a court since the Port Arthur massacre, Martin Bryant, the 29-year-old Tasmanian charged with 35 killings at the former convict settlement in April last year, will appear in the Hobart Supreme Court today surounded by unprecedented security. Page 3.

New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger told the Channel 7 Face to Face program last night he thought Australia was not as committed to competition as New Zealand, criticising Australia for a lack of dedication to free trade with his country. Page 3.

A confronting review of all police records from the investigation into the murder of 14-year-old Leigh Leigh prepared by Mrs Leigh's lawyers, has concluded there is a real possibility more youths were involved in the murder at the North Stockton Surf Club than the one convicted and charged. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following an alarming draft report by 40 of the world's leading global change experts, Australia will come under increasing international pressure to cut its greenhouse gas emissions. The report warns that the planet's forests will soon be unable to absor any more of the gases. Page 1.

Ten-year-old Sarah Otto was the only person left alive when a cliff face collapsed at Gracetown in Western Australia last week, killing four children and five adults. One hundred civilians, police and emergency workers scraped frantically with their bare hands until they dragged Sarah from the rubble. Page 1.

A decade after nine-year-old Samantha Knight disappeared from Bondi, police have uncovered new evidence after a witness reported a conversation with a man about Samantha which the witness thought was suspicious. Police interviewed the man last June and it is believed he had photographs of Samantha and her friends. Page 2.

In changes to be announced today, hoped to establish the supremacy of the Premier's Department in the management of the Australian Public Service, investment projects and politically sensitive issues, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has announced he will be turning the Premier's Department into a super agency with powers to force other departments to comply. Page 3.
THE AGE

10-year-old Sarah Otto was the only one to survive the landslide of earth and rock that killed nine people in Western Australia on Friday. Civilians, police and emergency service workers battled side-by-side to save her life, while her mother, four childen and four other adults lay dead beneath the mound of earth. Page A1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday called for the scrapping of the National Crime Authority, Queensland's Criminal Justice Commission and the New South Wales Independent Commission Against Corruption, claiming such authorities were costing State and Federal Governments millions of dollars a year to run. Page A1.

The Victorian gay community can afford to be cautiously optimistic following a wave of significant victories in the past month, including the self-outing of two members of the Uniting Church's clergy and the reluctant endorsement of a national report on sexuality by the Victorian synod. The Port Phillip City Council has also announced plans to establish a committee to ensure gays and lesbians have equitable access to municipal services. Page A1.

Defending his private members bill to overturn the Northern Territory euthanasia laws, Federal Liberal MP Kevin Andrews said yesterday that increasing health and pension costs would pressure the elderly into opting for voluntary euthanasia because they would feel they had become a burden. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
